units.t: Statistics: Tally Charts and Frequency Tables

unit.title: Chance
unit.blurb: Using words such as 'will happen', 'might happen' and 'will not happen' to describe chance, and doing simple chance experiments.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use the language of chance: will happen, might happen, will not happen.

O2.t: Carry out simple chance experiments and record the results.

p: Some things **will happen** (the sun will set today). Some things **might happen** (it might rain). Some things **will not happen** (a cat will fly).
If a bag has only red cubes, you **will** pick red. If it has red and blue, you **might** pick red.
Some events are certain, some impossible, and most are in between. Words like likely and unlikely describe how often we expect something to happen.

lesson.q: A bag has 9 red balls and 1 blue ball. Describe the chance of taking a red ball.
steps: Red is very likely but not certain

lesson.t: Describe the chance of an event
p: Think: can it happen at all?
If in between, decide: unlikely, even chance or likely.
If there are other colours in the bag, red only might happen.

p: In a **chance experiment** we try something many times and **record** what happens, often with tally marks.
If you flip a coin 10 times, you might get 4 heads and 6 tails. The results can change each time you try.
One try can give any result. Doing an experiment many times shows which results happen more often.

lesson.q: A coin is flipped 20 times and lands on heads 11 times. Is that surprising?
lesson.a: No – it is what we expect for a fair coin

p: Decide what you will do and record.
Repeat it many times and tally the results.
Compare the results with what you expected.
If you try again, you may get different results.
